page.title: Customer Community Strategy Checklist
page.description: A practical checklist covering platform choice, governance, programming, moderation, metrics and budget so you can launch or fix a customer community.
page.h1: What belongs on a customer community strategy checklist?
page.definition: A customer community strategy checklist is a structured set of decisions and deliverables that guides the launch or overhaul of a branded member space, covering platform selection, governance roles, content programming, moderation workflows, success metrics and budget allocation.
page.quick_answer: Start with a 90-day plan, pick one platform from Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic or LinkedIn groups, assign owners for moderation and programming, and track owned-audience growth each month.

sections.h2: Which platform fits our member volume and moderation risk?

blocks.p: Match the tool to the scale and risk profile of the community rather than defaulting to a familiar name.

head: Platform type
Best fit
rows: High-velocity chat, developer or peer-support communities
Course-driven or membership communities needing structured spaces
SEO-rich, long-form Q&A with strong search needs
Low-friction professional networking with existing audience

sections.h2: What governance roles and owners do we need from day one?

blocks.p: Assign a single owner to each workstream so accountability is clear before the first member joins.

ul: Community strategist: sets goals, roadmap and success metrics
Platform administrator: configures permissions, integrations and SSO
Moderation lead: writes guidelines, trains moderators and handles escalations
Programming manager: plans events, AMAs, content drops and rituals
Member success lead: owns onboarding, health scoring and churn alerts
Reporting analyst: builds dashboards for activity, sentiment and owned-audience growth

sections.h2: How do we structure programming that drives repeat participation?

blocks.p: Design a recurring calendar that mixes live moments with asynchronous value so members form a habit.

ol: Weekly: themed discussion thread or office-hours AMA
Bi-weekly: live workshop or expert interview streamed on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard
Monthly: member spotlight or case-study roundtable
Quarterly: virtual summit or hybrid meet-up produced with a run of show, speaker brief, rehearsal, branded slides, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream and edited clips
Ongoing: resource library updated with templates, playbooks and searchable FAQs

sections.h2: What moderation workflow keeps the space safe without bottlenecks?

blocks.p: Define escalation paths, response-time targets and tooling before the first conflict appears.

ul: Publish community guidelines and a visible code of conduct
Tier-one: automated keyword filters and member reporting
Tier-two: volunteer moderators with documented playbooks for common scenarios
Tier-three: paid moderation lead or agency coverage for high-risk hours and legal escalations
Weekly moderation retrospective to update playbooks and surface trends

sections.h2: Which metrics prove the community is growing owned audience?

blocks.p: Track indicators that map directly to email subscribers and community members rather than vanity followers.

head: Metric
Why it matters
rows: Shows habit formation and repeat participation
Quantifies cost savings for the business

sections.h2: How do we budget for community as a service versus in-house build?

blocks.p: Separate fixed platform costs from variable people costs and decide what to keep in-house versus outsource.

ul: Keep in-house: strategy, brand voice approval, product decisions
Outsource: moderation coverage, member support, programming execution, onboarding flows, monthly reporting
Platform licence: per-seat or tiered pricing from Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic
People cost: community manager salary or agency retainer scoped by coverage hours, member volume and moderation risk
Event production: moderated webinars from $2,500 per production; summits and hybrid events from $10,000 and above

faq.q: How long before we know if the community strategy is working?
faq.a: A first plan runs 90 days: long enough to see a trend in active members, activation rate and owned-audience growth, short enough to change course if metrics stall.

faq.q: Should we start on a free platform or buy enterprise tooling immediately?
faq.a: Start with the lowest-friction tool that matches your moderation risk; migrate to Khoros or Higher Logic only when compliance, analytics or scale demand it.

faq.q: What is the minimum viable moderation team for launch?
faq.a: One moderation lead with a documented playbook, two trained volunteer moderators for core hours, and an escalation path to legal or HR for high-risk issues.

faq.q: How do we turn event attendees into community members?
faq.a: Capture registration emails, invite attendees to a dedicated community space during the live event, and follow up within 24 to 48 hours with the replay and a threaded discussion prompt.

faq.q: When does West Peek Productions get involved in community work?
faq.a: West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations; community-as-a-service scoping covers coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming.
